ANA and NYR look close on the numbers that matter. At five on five, ANA has taken 47% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games and NYR 51%, so there isn't much between them. The model projects 3.17 goals for NYR tonight and 2.99 for ANA. On special teams, NYR takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays, though its penalty kill allows just 0.51 expected goals a game to ANA's 0.69.

In net, projected starter Dylan Garand (NYR) is on a heater: .955 over his last five starts, with 5.6 goals saved above expected (how many more shots he stopped than an average goalie would have). Over six games this season he sits at +2.9, with Igor Shesterkin on injured reserve. Projected ANA starter Lukas Dostal is at +0.7 this season after -3.71 across 56 games last year. Recent form leans toward ANA: 2-3-0 in its last five but with 52% of the expected goals, while NYR is 2-2-1 with 48%.

Among players to watch, Alexis Lafrenière (NYR) has a 34% chance to score, as does Beckett Sennecke (ANA). Mika Zibanejad (NYR) is tagged as a top power play option, which matters given NYR's penalty habit. Mikael Granlund is day-to-day but could return for ANA, while Ryan Poehling remains out with a lower-body injury. Frank Vatrano plays his 700th NHL game, a milestone the model doesn't price.
